rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is read with either hamza kasra or fatḥa; the fatḥ reading coordinates with ‘that you do not hunger.’
rows.anchor: قرىء ( وإنك ) بالكسر والفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāw can stand for any governing particle, not just إن, so it can precede أن although إن itself cannot.
rows.anchor: الواو لم توضع لتكون أبدا نائبة عن إن ، إنما هي نائبة عن كل عامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food, drink, clothing, and shade are life’s basic needs; Paradise fully provides Adam without requiring another provider or worldly earnings.
rows.anchor: الشبع والري والكسوة والكن : هي الأقطاب التي يدور عليها كفاف الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating the opposites names forms of misery Adam was warned against, so he would avoid their causes.
rows.anchor: وذكرها بلفظ النفي لنقائضها التي هي الجوع والعري والظمأ والضحو ، ليطرق سمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Adam after repentance and drew him near; ijtabā derives from gathering, as illustrated by gathering something and adorning a bride.
rows.anchor: من جبى إلي كذا فاجتبيته . ونظيره : جليت علي العروس فاجتليتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s guidance enabled Adam to preserve repentance and other means of protection and piety.
rows.anchor: أي وفقه لحفظ التوبة وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Eve are humanity’s two origins and are addressed as humanity in the plural, like assigning an effect’s act to its cause.
rows.anchor: لما كان آدم وحواء عليهما السلام أصلى البشر ، والسببين اللذين منها نشؤا وتفرعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance here means scripture and religious law.
rows.anchor: { هدى } كتاب وشريعة

words: فمن اتبع هداى فلا يضل ولا يشقى
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God guarantees that Qur’an followers will not stray in this world or suffer in the next; he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ضمن الله لمن اتبع القرآن أن لا يضل في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hereafter misery punishes those who strayed from religion in this life; following the Book and obeying it saves from error and punishment.
rows.anchor: أن الشقاء في الآخرة هو عقاب من ضل في الدنيا عن طريق الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍank is a verbal noun that describes either masculine or feminine nouns.
rows.anchor: مصدر يستوي في الوصف به المذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads ḍankā on the faʿlā pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ضنكى ) على فعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surrender, contentment, and trust in God’s allotment produce easy spending and a comfortable life; greed and miserliness constrict the life of one who turns from religion.
rows.anchor: مع الدين التسليم والقناعة والتوكل على الله وعلى قسمته

rows.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
rows.claim: An unnamed Sufi says turning from God darkens one’s time and unsettles one’s provision.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المتصوفة : لا يعرض أحد عن ذكر ربه إلا أظلم عليه وقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some unbelievers face humiliation for disbelief; other verses promise blessings for faith, obeying scripture, seeking forgiveness, and steadfastness.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى : { وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة وباءوا بغضب من الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the constricted life is al-Ḍarīʿ and al-Zaqqūm in Hell.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : هو الضريع والزقوم في النار

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī identifies it with punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري : ( 687 ) ( عذاب القبر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jussive ‘We gather him’ coordinates with the syntactic position of the conditional apodosis ‘he will have a constricted life.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء { ونحشره } بالجزم عطفا على محل { فإن له معيشة ضنكا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading gives hāʾ sukūn as in pausal pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ونحشره ) بسكون الهاء على لفظ الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blindness parallels 17:97; ‘just as’ means God treats the person as he treated the signs, leaving him blind.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل قوله : { ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s clear signs went unheeded; the person failed to reflect, abandoned them, and was blind to them, so God leaves him blind that day.
rows.anchor: آياتنا أتتك واضحة مستنيرة ، فلم تنظر إليها بعين المعتبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Devote yourself and your family to worship and prayer, use prayer to endure hardship, and leave provision to God to focus on the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي وأقبل أنت مع أهلك على عبادة الله والصلاة ؛ واستعينوا بها على خصاصتكم

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: Seeing rulers’ wealth, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr recited the warning against coveting it and called people to prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن عروة بن الزبير أنه كان إذا رأى ما عند السلاطين قرأ : { ولا تمدن عينيك }

rows.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله المزني
rows.claim: When his family was poor, Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī told them to get up and pray, citing God’s command to His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وعن بكر بن عبد الله المزني كان إذا أصابت أهله خصاصة قال : قوموا فصلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads ‘we are humiliated and disgraced’ in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: قرىء { نذل ونخزى } على لفظ ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both sides await the outcome of their respective affairs.
rows.anchor: أي كل واحد منا ومنكم { متربص } للعاقبة ولما يؤول إليه أمرنا وأمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sawāʾ is read as middle or best, even or upright, and with related forms glossed as diminutives of al-sūʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( السواء ) بمعنى الوسط والجيد . أو المستوى والسوء والسوأي والسوي تصغير السوء

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ says he memorized from the Prophet the variant ‘Enjoy yourselves; soon you will know.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون ) قال أبو رافع : حفظته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises a reciter of Ṭā-Hā the Resurrection reward of the Emigrants and Helpers; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A second report says Paradise’s people recite no Qur’an except Ṭā-Hā and Yā-Sīn; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقال : ( 690 ) ( لا يقرأ أهل الجنة من القرآن إلا طه ويس )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ is Meccan and has 112 verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآياتها اثنتا عشرة ومائة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading omits wāw in a-lam yaraw; ratqan is also read with fatḥa on tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرىء : { ألم يروا } بغير واو . و { رتقا } بفتح التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ratq and ratqan are understood as ‘joined’; ratq can stand for ‘a joined thing’ because it is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: كالخلق والنقض ، أي : كانتا مرتوقتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Views say the sky adhered to earth with no gap, or the heavens and earths were contiguous before God separated them.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ذلك : أن السماء كانت لاصقة بالأرض لا فضاء بينهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says rain and vegetation split the closed sky and earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ففتقناها بالمطر والنبات بعد ما كانت مصمتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual form refers to the groups of heavens and earths, as ‘two black herds’ means two groups.
rows.anchor: جماعة السموات وجماعة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an, itself miraculous, stands in place of observation; because either cosmic state is rationally possible, their differentiation requires a determining agent.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه وارد في القرآن الذي هو معجزة في نفسه ، فقام مقام المرئي المشاهد

words: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If jaʿalnā takes one object, God created every animal from water, as in 24:45, or living beings depend intensely on water; with two objects, water is the indispensable cause of life. The author also cites 21:37 for human haste.
rows.anchor: خلقنا من الماء كل حيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min can indicate causation, as in the quoted Prophetic phrase ‘I am not of dadd, nor is dadd of me.’
rows.anchor: و ( من ) هذا نحو ( من ) في قوله عليه السلام . ( 696 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads ḥayyan as the second object; the adverb is syntactically non-governing.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( حيا ) وهو المفعول الثاني . والظرف لغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means ‘for fear they sway’ or ‘lest they sway’; Kufans allow omission of lā and lām when unambiguous, as in 57:29.
rows.anchor: أي كراهة { أن تميد بهم } وتضطرب . أو لئلا تميد بهم ، فحذف ( لا ) واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fijāj means broad roads.
rows.anchor: الفج : الطريق الواسع . فإن قلت : في الفجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fijāj precedes subul as a circumstantial accusative, not an adjective; the cited line about ʿAzza’s ruin witnesses the construction.
rows.anchor: قلت : لم تقدم وهي صفة ، ولكن جعلت حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse says God made broad roads; 71:20 says He created the earth already characterized by them, explaining what was implicit here.
rows.anchor: أحدهما الإعلام بأنه جعل فيها طرقا واسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is protected from falling or quaking by God’s power, or from demons eavesdropping by meteors.
rows.anchor: محفوظا حفظه بالإمساك بقدرته من أن يقع على الأرض ويتزلزل ، أو بالشهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs include celestial lights and their ordered courses, risings, and settings, displaying divine wisdom and power.
rows.anchor: عن ءاياتها } أي عما وضع الله فيها من الأدلة والعبر بالشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A singular reading suffices to signify the class of signs.
rows.anchor: اكتفاء بالواحدة في الدلالة على الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People notice worldly benefits from the sky but ignore it as a clear sign of the Creator.
rows.anchor: هم متفطنون لما يرد عليهم من السماء من المنافع الدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uff is an exclamation whose sound signals irritation.
rows.anchor: صوت إذا صوت به علم أن صاحبه متضجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was exasperated by their persistence after their excuse ended and truth became clear; the lām marks those he was annoyed with.
rows.anchor: ثباتهم على عبادتها بعد انقطاع عذرهم وبعد وضوح الحق وزهوق الباطل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Dhū al-Kifl is variously identified as Elijah, Zechariah, or Joshua son of Nun.
rows.anchor: قيل في ذي الكفل : هو إلياس . وقيل : زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may be called Dhū al-Kifl as one allotted a share from God and truly fortunate; another report says his work and reward were doubled.
rows.anchor: وكأنه سمي بذلك لأنه ذو الحظ من الله والمجدود على الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Five prophets are said to have two names: Israel/Jacob, Elijah/Dhū al-Kifl, Jesus/the Messiah, Jonah/Dhū al-Nūn, and Muḥammad/Aḥmad.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خمسة من الأنبياء ذوو اسمين : إسرائيل ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nūn means whale, to which Dhū al-Nūn is attributed.
rows.anchor: الحوت ، فأضيف إليه . برم بقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah wearied of his unbelieving people and left angry, thinking zeal for God justified it, but should have waited for permission to migrate; he was tested in the whale.
rows.anchor: برم بقومه لطول ما ذكرهم فلم يذكروا وأقاموا على كفرهم ، فراغمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he angered his people by leaving while they feared punishment would descend.
rows.anchor: ومعنى مغاضبته لقومه : أنه أغضبهم بمفارقته

rows.speaker: أبو شرف
rows.claim: Abū Sharaf reads mughḍaban.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو شرف ( مغضبا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb has light and heavy forms, a light yāʾ reading, and passive readings with either consonant weight.
rows.anchor: ويقدر ، بالياء بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is interpreted as constricting Jonah or decreeing punishment; the light reading can mean not exercising power over him.
rows.anchor: وفسرت بالتضييق عليه ، وبتقدير الله عليه عقوبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās asks Muʿāwiya about the verse after being overwhelmed by it; Muʿāwiya says it concerns divine decree, not power.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : أنه دخل على معاوية فقال : لقد ضربتني أمواج القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light reading may be figurative; alternatively Satan’s whisper arose and Jonah rejected it by proof, as believers do, as in 33:10.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون من باب التمثيل ، بمعنى : فكانت حاله ممثلة بحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darkness was inside the whale, compared with imagery in 2:17 and 2:257.
rows.anchor: في الظلمة الشديدة المتكاثفة في بطن الحوت ، كقوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view counts the whale’s belly, sea, and night as the darknesses.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ظلمات بطن الحوت والبحر والليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another says a larger whale swallowed Jonah’s whale, adding two belly-darknesses to the sea’s darkness.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ابتلع حوته حوت أكبر منه ، فحصل في ظلمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle can mean ‘that’ or act as the explanatory ‘namely.’
rows.anchor: أي بأنه { لا إلاه إلا أنت } أو بمعنى ( أي )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says no distressed person who invokes this supplication will fail to receive an answer; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ما من مكروب يدعو بهذا الدعاء إلا استجيب له

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Jonah was saved only by admitting his wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : ما نجاه والله إلا إقراره على نفسه بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The governing phrase for ‘the day We fold the sky’ may be ‘they will not grieve,’ ‘the terror,’ or ‘they will be received.’
rows.anchor: لا يحزنهم . أو الفزع . أو تتلقاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads the sky is folded in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( تطوى السماء ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sijill is read on the pattern of ʿutul or like the word for a bucket; a kasra reading is also reported.
rows.anchor: و { السجل } بوزن العتل والسجل بلفظ الدلو . وروي فيه الكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sijill means scroll or sheet; folding it resembles folding a scroll for writing or one bearing writing. Kitāb began as a verbal noun before denoting written material.
rows.anchor: وهو الصحيفة ، أي : كما يطوى الطومار للكتابة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes al-Sijill an angel who folds Adam’s descendants’ records when given them.
rows.anchor: وقيل { السجل } : ملك يطوي كتب بني آدم إذا رفعت إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes al-Sijill a scribe of the Prophet; then ‘book’ means the written sheet.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كاتب كان لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Re-creation parallels origination: both bring beings from nonexistence, and God’s power applies equally to each.
rows.anchor: نعيد أول الخلق كما بدأناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq is indefinite and singular like ‘the first man who came,’ meaning creatures considered one by one; as a verbal noun it has no plural.
rows.anchor: هو كقولك : هو أول رجل جاءني ، تريد أول الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kāf is governed by an implied verb explained by nuʿīdu, mā is relative, and awwal khalq is adverbial or circumstantial.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر ، وهو أن ينتصب الكاف بفعل مضمر يفسره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waʿdan is an emphatic verbal noun; ‘We are doing it’ means God is able to re-create.
rows.anchor: أي قادرين على أن نفعل ذلك

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī identifies al-Zabūr as David’s Psalms and al-dhikr as the Torah.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي رحمة الله عليه : زبور داود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Al-dhikr may mean the scriptures generally or the Mother Book, the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وقيل اسم لجنس ما أنزل على الأنبياء من الكتب . والذكر : أم الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says believers inherit earth after unbelievers are expelled, as in 7:137 and Moses’ statement in 7:128.
rows.anchor: أي : يرثها المؤمنون بعد إجلاء الكفار ، كقوله تعالى : { وأورثنا القوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the earth is Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : هي أرض الجنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the Holy Land will be inherited by Muḥammad’s community.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الأرض المقدسة ، ترثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing tafath includes trimming moustache and nails, plucking armpit hair, and shaving pubic hair; tafath means dirt to be removed.
rows.anchor: قضاء التفث : قص الشارب والأظفار ونتف الإبط والاستحداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading doubles the fāʾ in yuwafū.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وليوفوا ) بتشديد الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vows mean pilgrimage obligations or pious acts vowed during pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: مواجب حجهم ، أو ما عسى ينذرونه من أعمال البر في حجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred view is Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍa/Ziyāra, a pillar of pilgrimage that completes release from consecration.
rows.anchor: طواف الإفاضة ، وهو طواف الزيارة الذي هو من أركان الحج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the circumambulation as the farewell Ṭawāf al-Ṣadr.
rows.anchor: وقيل : طواف الصدر ، وهو طواف الوداع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says al-ʿAtīq means ancient, since the House was the first established for people.
rows.anchor: العتيق } القديم ، لأنه أول بيت وضع للناس عن الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says it is freed from tyrants, whom God prevented from destroying it.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : أعتق من الجبابرة ، كم من جبار سار إليه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the House was never owned; another report from him says it was saved from the flood.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : لم يملك قط . وعنه : أعتق من الغرق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view means ‘noble house,’ from the phrase for noble horses or birds.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بيت كريم ، من قولهم : عتاق الخيل والطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥajjāj targeted Ibn al-Zubayr, who had fortified himself at the House, then rebuilt it after removing him; when Abraha targeted it, God dealt with him as He did.
rows.anchor: ما قصد التسلط على البيت ، وإنما تحصن به ابن الزبير ، فاحتال لإخراجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika predicates an omitted subject, ‘the matter is this,’ like a writer’s transition to a new topic.
rows.anchor: { ذالك } خبر مبتدأ محذوف ، أي : الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥurma cannot be violated; protected obligations may be all divine duties or specifically pilgrimage rites.
rows.anchor: والحرمة : ما لا يحل هتكه . وجميع ما كلفه الله تعالى بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam lists the Kaaba, Sacred Mosque, territory, sacred month, and pilgrim in consecration among five sanctities.
rows.anchor: وعن زيد بن أسلم : الحرمات خمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Veneration benefits the person and means knowing sanctities must be respected, protected, and observed.
rows.anchor: أي فالتعظيم خير له . ومعنى التعظيم : العلم بأنها واجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception refers to a recited prohibition, 5:3, not livestock itself; do not forbid lawful animals or permit forbidden ones.
rows.anchor: المتلو لا يستثنى من الأنعام ، ولكن المعنى { إلا ما يتلى عليكم } آية تحريمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to shun idols and falsehood follows reverence because monotheism and truth are the greatest sanctities.
rows.anchor: لما حث على تعظيم حرماته وأحمد من يعظمها أتبعه الأمر باجتناب الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is falsehood because idolaters claim idols deserve worship; avoid idol worship as the chief falsehood and all false speech.
rows.anchor: لأن المشرك زاعم أن الوثن تحق له العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols, like wine, gambling, and divining arrows, are called filth by analogy; 5:90 gives avoidance of filth as the reason.
rows.anchor: وسمى الأوثان رجسا وكذلك الخمر والميسر والأزلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min al-awthān specifies the otherwise broad term rij’s, like specifying a number as dirhams.
rows.anchor: من الأوثان } بيان للرجس وتمييز له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zūr is linked to deviation and ifk to turning aside; reported senses include declaring lawful what is forbidden and false testimony.
rows.anchor: والزور والأزورار وهو الانحراف ، كما أن الإفك من أفكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qad affirms an expected outcome while lammā denies it; it establishes the success believers awaited.
rows.anchor: قد أفلح المؤمنون } نقيضه ( لما ) هي تثبت المتوقع و ( لما ) تنفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falāḥ means attaining one’s aim or remaining in goodness; aflaḥa means entering success, and aflaḥahu making someone succeed.
rows.anchor: والفلاح : الظفر بالمراد ، وقيل : البقاء في الخير

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa reads aflaḥa passive, aflaḥū by the ‘akalūnī al-barāghīth’ construction or ellipsis, and aflaḥ with ḍamma instead of wāw, supported by poetry.
rows.anchor: وعليه قراءة طلحة بن مصرف : أفلح ، على البناء للمفعول . وعنه : ( أفلحوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In language, a believer is one who confirms.
rows.anchor: قلت : هو في اللغة المصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One legal view counts anyone professing the testimonies with heart and tongue aligned as a believer; another reserves the praise for the righteous and pious, excluding sinners.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن كل من نطق بالشهادتين مواطئا قلبه لسانه فهو مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility in prayer is fear in the heart and lowering one’s gaze to the prostration place.
rows.anchor: الخشوع في الصلاة : خشية القلب وإلباد البصر عن قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda defines humility as fixing one’s gaze on the prostration place.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة : وهو إلزامه موضع السجود

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet lowered his gaze to his prayer place after this verse was revealed; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 717 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scholar feared the Merciful enough to keep his gaze still and avoid worldly thoughts; another view is focused attention and turning from everything else.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل من العلماء إذا قام إلى الصلاة هاب الرحمن أن يشد بصره إلى شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer manners include avoiding gathered clothing, fidgeting, looking around, stretching, yawning, eye-closing, mouth-covering, letting garments hang, cracking joints, interlocking fingers, akhtiṣār, and turning pebbles.
rows.anchor: ومن الخشوع : أن يستعمل الآداب ، فيتوقى كف الثوب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told a man fidgeting with his beard that humble hearts make humble limbs; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 718 ) أنه أبصر رجلا يعبث بلحيته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan rebuked a man asking for a bride from the houris while fidgeting with pebbles, calling him a bad suitor.
rows.anchor: ونظر الحسن إلى رجل يعبث بالحصا وهو يقول : اللهم زوجني الحور العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is attributed to worshippers because they alone benefit; it is their provision and treasure, while God needs and gains nothing from it.
rows.anchor: فالمصلي هو المنتفع بها وحده
